q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(CAST(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS) AS DECIMAL(10,2))/CAST(COUNT(EMPLOYEE_ID) AS DECIMAL(10,2)),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM( SELECT PROJECT_ID, P.EMPLOYEE_ID, EXPERIENCE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID=E. EMPLOYEE_ID ) AS SUB GROUP BY PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 calculates the average experience years for each project by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of employees in that project. On the other hand, Q2 calculates the average experience years for each project by first summing up the experience years of all employees in the project and then dividing by the number of employees in that project. The difference arises when an employee is assigned to multiple projects, as Q1 and Q2 handle this case differently.
counterexample_dsp: Create a scenario where an employee is assigned to two projects. Q1 will count this employee's experience years twice when calculating the average for each project, while Q2 will sum up the experience years only once and divide by the number of projects the employee is assigned to.
